Aisha R: BankEdge convo: they want a 2-week POC to validate streaming SDK + function-calls behind Okta & corporate proxy. Need: SSO flow notes, low-p95 batching recommendations, reserved-capacity ballpark for ~200 qps, and a tiny Go adapter example. Who can own?

Diego M: I can handle SSO + proxy advice. We support SP-initiated SAML with Okta. For proxies that terminate TLS, we need their CA bundle and proxy IPs to troubleshoot streaming. Recommend short-lived ephemeral tokens swapped via backend to avoid embedding creds in client.

Nina S: Performance quick notes: for sub-100ms p95 use continuous batching with max_batch_latency=10ms and max_batch_size=48 on rwd-medium for avg 3-5k tokens. If they want lower cost, increase latency to 25ms and size to 128 which cuts per-token cost ~15%. Also enable KV prefix cache for repeated prompts. I'll put numbers in the runbook.

Aisha R: Pricing ask: sustained 200 qps. Need 1yr vs 3yr committed pricing options and a recommended GPU reserve.

Diego M: Thumb estimate: 200 qps * 120 tokens = ~24k tps. For predictable latency recommend Dedicated pool ~4 A100-equivalents with 20% headroom and autoscale. Exact quote from finance.

Presales Bot: Runbook created -> https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/presales/bankedge-mini-poc (checklist: Okta metadata, proxy CA, network egress, sample app).

Aisha R: Can someone paste a minimal Go snippet for ephemeral token exchange + starting an SSE stream with function calls for the infra team? One page max.

Nina S: Tiny Go sketch:
```go
// exchange ephemeral token
resp, _ := http.Post("https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/ephemeral","application/json",bytes.NewBuffer(body))
token, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
// start SSE stream
req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET","https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=rwd-medium&functions=1",nil)
req.Header.Set("Authorization","Bearer "+string(token))
client.Do(req)
```. Full sample repo linked in runbook.
